text:
maya: seeing intermittent packet loss on the VXLAN overlay in the gpu-prod pool (us-west-2). Symptoms: short bursts of drops & retransmits during large gradient syncs, latency spikes ~100-400ms for a few seconds, then back to normal. same-node pod pairs look fine, cross-node traffic affected. noticed it around 03:45 UTC tonight.

ops-bot: alert: cluster/gpu-prod: overlay_loss_rate > 0.5% (3 hosts) — triggered 2025-11-18T03:46:02Z

ravi: which nodes and NICs? kernel + driver versions? is this geneve or vxlan?

maya: vxlan (default cilium tunnel) on nodes: gpu-west-01/02/07. kernels: 5.10.147, mlx5 driver v5.11. captured some tcp retransmits in app logs.

joel: quick checks: tc -s qdisc show dev vxlan_sys_4789, ethtool -k eth0, and ethtool -S for mlx counters. Also check if tunnel offload is on (can create large skbs that NIC offload mishandles).

elaine: we've hit this before: VXLAN + GRO/GSO + NIC offloads can cause mid-burst drops when large skbs get split/rewritten. Often shows up only at high throughput (allreduce). Try toggling GRO/GSO on the vxlan/veth and see if drops stop.

yun: agree. also run: 
```
iperf3 -c <peer> -t 30 -P 8
sudo tcpdump -i vxlan_sys_4789 -w /tmp/vxlan.pcap
sudo tc -s qdisc show dev vxlan_sys_4789
```
collect on both ends simultaneously.

maya: running iperf now between gpu-west-01 -> gpu-west-02, will attach pcap. baseline throughput good but during training bursts we see retransmits.

joel: temp mitigations to try: 
 - ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
 - ethtool -K vxlan_sys_4789 gro off
 - set MTU to 1400 on cilium veths/tunnels
 - change qdisc to fq or fq_codel if not set: tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq
these are low-risk and quick to test.

maya: tried disabling GRO on vxlan on gpu-west-02: drops dropped from ~1.2% -> 0.03% during a 10m sync. promising.

ravi: OK that's a good sign — likely offload/tunnel interaction. If disabling GRO helps, we should consider a safer cluster-wide config: either set MTU down or disable tunnel offload at CNI level, or pin to NIC driver version with the tunnel-offload fix.

elaine: also check conntrack and kube-proxy mode. If conntrack is overloaded it can amplify retransmit symptoms. run: sudo conntrack -S and /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max.

yun: another thing: check ethtool -k shows tcp-segmentation-offload and scatter-gather. mlx5 had a firmware bug a while back that mis-handled segmented pkts with vxlan. Vendor recommended disabling tunnel offload until firmware patched.

joel: longer-term options: kernel upgrade (newer tunnel-offload patches), NIC firmware update, or move to native eBPF-based routing without encapsulation for these GPU nodes (we can enable policy-based hairpin/underlay for intra-pool traffic).

maya: action plan:
 - (maya) capture pcap + tc stats from 3 affected nodes during next job (ETA 2h)
 - (ravi) check NIC firmware and driver changelog for mlx5 tunnel fixes, open ticket with vendor if needed (ETA EOD)
 - (joel) draft safe rollout: cluster-wide gro/gso toggle via daemonset + canary on 10% of gpu nodes (tomorrow)
 - (elaine) check conntrack usage and kube-proxy mode, report back (ETA 6h)

ops-bot: incident created: INFRA-2025-622: intermittent-vxlan-loss — severity: medium — owner: maya

maya: attaching one sample tcpdump snippet here (trimmed):
```
# tcpdump -nn -r /tmp/vxlan.pcap | head -n 20
09:45:12.123456 IP 10.244.1.12.50012 > 10.244.2.34.50012: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12500, ack 98765, win 29200, length 155
09:45:12.124789 IP 10.244.1.12 > 10.244.2.34: ICMP echo request, id 1, seq 12, length 64
09:45:12.125345 IP 10.244.1.12.50012 > 10.244.2.34.50012: Flags [.], ack 98766, win 29200, length 0
# lots of retransmits around 09:45:12.12x
```

ravi: good. once we have vendor confirmation we can plan firmware/driver work. For GA-critical jobs let's keep GRO off for the gpu pool until resolved. Cost: a small perf hit but saves retries.

joel: note perf hit mostly shows up for small-packet throughput; for our large model syncs it might be ~5-8% CPU/network overhead but acceptable vs packet loss.

maya: I'll roll the daemonset that disables GRO on vxlan for the gpu-prod pool as a canary in 30m and post results.

elaine: +1. please include a toggle so we can revert quickly. Also document in runbooks the commands and metrics to watch (retransmit rate, tc drops, ethtool stats).

maya: will update runbook and ping when canary completes. thanks all :pray:
